PRODUCT OVERVIEW

A tipper enquiry starts with the load and the unloading task.

For loose bulk cargo, describe the material, its density or weight per trip, and the unloading site. Cargo type, discharge direction and body arrangement require checking against the actual task and model, rather than choosing from an appearance image alone.

This page lists nine tipper and flatbed-tipper models. For example, EHJ9400ZHX has an approved gross mass of 40000 kg and listed rated payloads of 31500, 31800 and 32270 kg. Vehicle length and curb mass vary by model.

APPLICATION & SELECTION

Turn your application into selection criteria

Discuss the actual transport task first, then check the corresponding model and equipment.

01

Describe the cargo first

Provide the cargo type and form, moisture or sticking characteristics, and planned weight per trip. Suitability for materials such as aggregates or coal needs confirmation for the particular body and model.

02

Confirm discharge and site conditions

State whether rear or side discharge is needed, along with unloading equipment, space and access conditions. Confirm the discharge arrangement, lifting equipment and operating requirements for the chosen model.

03

Compare weight and length together

Gross mass is not payload. Compare the chosen model’s rated payload, curb mass and length options together. Do not assume that the longest body and a listed payload can be combined into one configuration.

Mainly carrying general cargo? Compare the flatbed and drop-side series.

PREPARE YOUR ENQUIRY

Prepare these four details for your enquiry

Specific information helps us compare models and configurations. Price, availability and the final proposal are confirmed through the enquiry.

Material and load

Material name, photos, form or density, sticking characteristics and planned weight per trip.

Discharge and site

Discharge direction, site photos, available space, operating equipment and access-road conditions.

Tractor and equipment

Tractor model and coupling details, information on existing hydraulic or related equipment, and operating region.

Preferred configuration

Preferred model and length, tire and suspension requirements, quantity and intended in-service date.

You can start with the cargo and operating task; sales will help identify a model and configuration. If a model is already chosen, provide its complete code rather than only the category.
